groups.name: Acyl Halides & Acid Chlorides
groups.description: Highly reactive organic acid halides (e.g., Sebacoyl chloride, Acetyl chloride) that undergo violent nucleophilic acyl substitution.

groups.name: Halogenated Organic Compounds
groups.description: Chlorinated/brominated hydrocarbons (e.g., Dichloromethane, Chloroform) sensitive to active metals and caustics; persistent environmental toxins.

groups.name: Water-Reactive Substances
groups.description: Substances that react violently with moisture, generating toxic/corrosive gases or intense exothermic heat.

groups.name: Water & Aqueous Solutions
groups.description: Water, aqueous buffers, saline, and water-based pharmaceutical formulations.

groups.name: Strong Oxidizing Agents
groups.description: Electron acceptors (e.g., Nitric acid, Hydrogen peroxide, Potassium permanganate) capable of causing runaway combustion with organics.

groups.name: Strong Reducing Agents
groups.description: Substances (e.g., Sodium borohydride, Hydrides, Sulfites, Basic Chromium Sulfate) that release flammable hydrogen or react violently with oxidizers.

groups.name: Inorganic / Mineral Acids
groups.description: Strong mineral acids (e.g., Sulfuric acid, Hydrochloric acid, Nitric acid) that violently neutralize bases and protonate sulfides.

groups.name: Organic / Carboxylic Acids
groups.description: Carbon-based acids (e.g., Formic acid, Acetic acid, Glycolic acid, Citric acid) that react exothermically with bases and protonate sulfides.

groups.name: Caustics & Strong Bases
groups.description: Alkaline compounds (e.g., Sodium hydroxide, Calcium hydroxide lime, Potassium hydroxide) that react violently with acids and acyl halides.

groups.name: Alcohols & Polyols
groups.description: Hydroxy compounds (e.g., Ethanol, Isopropanol, Phenoxyethanol, Glycerol) susceptible to rapid esterification and flammability.

groups.name: Amines & Nitrogenous Bases
groups.description: Organic amines and amino compounds (e.g., Triethanolamine, Amoxicillin, Piperidine) acting as nucleophiles.

groups.name: Cyanides & Nitriles
groups.description: Cyanide salts and organic nitriles capable of releasing lethal Hydrogen Cyanide (HCN) gas under acidic conditions.

groups.name: Sulfides & Hydrosulfides
groups.description: Inorganic/organic sulfides (e.g., Sodium sulfide Na2S, NaHS) that release rapid lethal Hydrogen Sulfide (H2S) gas upon contact with acids.

groups.name: Peroxides & Hydroperoxides
groups.description: Unstable O-O bond compounds (e.g., Hydrogen peroxide 35%) prone to catalytic decomposition, violent oxidation, and runaway exotherm.

groups.name: Flammable & Combustible Solvents
groups.description: Low-flashpoint organic solvents (e.g., Toluene, Acetone, Limonene, Ethanol) presenting severe fire and explosion hazards.

groups.name: Cytotoxic & Antineoplastic Agents
groups.description: Genotoxic, mutagenic, or teratogenic antineoplastic pharmaceuticals (e.g., Cisplatin, Methotrexate) governed by USP <800>.

matrix.hazardTitle: FATAL ACCIDENT HAZARD: Instantaneous Lethal Hydrogen Sulfide (H2S) Gas Release
matrix.description: Contact between inorganic sulfides (e.g., Sodium sulfide) and mineral acids (Sulfuric, Hydrochloric, Nitric) causes instantaneous liberation of lethal Hydrogen Sulfide (H2S) gas. H2S causes immediate olfactory nerve paralysis, pulmonary edema, rapid respiratory arrest, and death within 1-2 breaths at >500 ppm.
matrix.segregationAction: MANDATORY ISOLATION: Store in separate dedicated bays with minimum 6 meters distance or a fire-rated barrier. Sulfide stores must have continuous H2S gas sensors with audible alarm interlocking to emergency scrubbers. NEVER co-mingle wastewater streams.
matrix.emergencyPrecautions: Evacuate area immediately upwind. Wear positive-pressure SCBA. Do not enter without breathing apparatus. Neutralize spills strictly with alkaline oxidizing bleach solution (pH > 11), NEVER with acid.
matrix.authoritativeSource: NOAA CAMEO Chemicals / OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1200 / Tannery Safety Directive

matrix.hazardTitle: Lethal Hydrogen Sulfide (H2S) Gas Generation via Organic Acid Protonation
matrix.description: Organic carboxylic acids (Formic acid, Acetic acid, Glycolic acid) rapidly protonate sulfide salts, releasing toxic H2S gas and flammable organic fumes. Common fatal occurrence during leather pickling or deliming if liming liquor residue is present.
matrix.segregationAction: Segregate organic acids in an acid-proof chemical store physically separated from sodium sulfide and liming chemical pallets.
matrix.emergencyPrecautions: Monitor air with portable multi-gas detector. Ensure continuous ventilation in leather drum unloading bays.
matrix.authoritativeSource: NOAA CAMEO Chemicals / Leather Technologists & Chemists Association Guide

matrix.hazardTitle: Violent Hydrolysis, Pressure Blowout & Choking HCl Acid Release
matrix.description: Acyl halides react violently and exothermically with water or moisture, generating boiling corrosive liquid spray and dense clouds of toxic, choking Hydrogen Chloride (HCl) gas. In sealed drums, the sudden pressure surge causes vessel rupture.
matrix.segregationAction: Store strictly under desiccated, moisture-free nitrogen blankets. NEVER dispose into aqueous waste sinks, floor drains, or wet carboys.
matrix.emergencyPrecautions: Use anhydrous soda ash or dry sand for spills. Avoid water sprays directly on spill.
matrix.authoritativeSource: NOAA CAMEO Chemicals / Prudent Practices in the Laboratory (NRC)

matrix.chemicalEquation: R-COCl + 2 NaOH -> R-COONa + NaCl + H2O + Extreme Heat
matrix.description: Mixing strong caustics directly with acyl halides causes an uncontrollable thermal explosion. The rapid temperature spike instantly vaporizes volatile liquids and propels caustic droplets.
matrix.segregationAction: Strict physical segregation. Controlled neutralization requires chilled jacketed reactors with dropwise stoichiometric addition.
matrix.emergencyPrecautions: Full chemical splash suit, neoprene apron, face shield, and chemical-resistant footwear required.
matrix.authoritativeSource: NOAA CAMEO Chemicals / Bretherick's Handbook of Reactive Chemical Hazards

matrix.hazardTitle: Rapid Exothermic Esterification & Anhydrous HCl Overpressurization
matrix.description: Spontaneous reaction between acyl halides and alcohols releases substantial heat and anhydrous HCl gas, causing extreme pressure buildup in closed waste drums.
matrix.segregationAction: Segregate acyl halides completely from organic solvent/alcohol waste drums. Ensure waste drum has a pressure-relief safety cap.
matrix.emergencyPrecautions: Vent drum slowly under dry fume hood if pressurized. Isolate in dedicated halogenated/acidic carboy.
matrix.authoritativeSource: NOAA CAMEO Chemicals / EPA RCRA Handling Guidelines

matrix.description: Mixing strong mineral acids with caustics produces instantaneous thermal release capable of boiling liquid mixtures and generating corrosive aerosols.
matrix.segregationAction: Store in separate, dedicated, corrosion-proof polypropylene bunded cabinets (Blue = Acids, Red/White = Bases). Do not co-mingle without automated cooling.
matrix.emergencyPrecautions: Use separate secondary bunds. Never allow drainage trenches to cross between acid and base storage bays.
matrix.authoritativeSource: NOAA CAMEO Chemicals / NFPA 400 Hazardous Materials Code

matrix.chemicalEquation: CH2Cl2 + 2 NaOH -> HCHO + 2 NaCl + H2O + Toxic Decomposition Byproducts
matrix.description: Caustics react with halogenated organics (Dichloromethane, Chloroform) via base-catalyzed dehydrohalogenation. Can produce toxic carbenes, phosgene gas traces, or spontaneous explosion under warm conditions.
matrix.segregationAction: Never pour halogenated extraction solvents into caustic scrubbers or basic waste drums. Route DCM to Halogenated Solvent Drum.
matrix.emergencyPrecautions: If inadvertent mixing occurs, vent vapors to scrubber and cool vessel externally.
matrix.authoritativeSource: NOAA CAMEO Chemicals / ECHA Hazard Dossier

matrix.hazardTitle: Spontaneous Combustion, Flash Fire & Catastrophic Deflagration
matrix.chemicalEquation: 2 HNO3 + Organic Solvent -> Rapid Runaway Oxidation + NOx + Fire/Explosion
matrix.description: Contact between strong oxidizers (Nitric acid, H2O2, Permanganate) and flammable solvents (Toluene, Acetone, Ethanol, Limonene) produces spontaneous ignition and runaway oxidation deflagration.
matrix.segregationAction: Store oxidizers in dedicated oxidizer safety cabinets with at least 6 meters separation or fireproof partitions from flammable solvent stores. Never co-dispose into solvent drums.
matrix.emergencyPrecautions: Ensure deluge foam or water mist fire suppression systems in solvent and oxidizer storage bays.
matrix.authoritativeSource: NOAA CAMEO Chemicals / NFPA 30 Flammable Liquids Code

matrix.hazardTitle: Violent Redox Deflagration / Hexavalent Chromium Formation Hazard
matrix.chemicalEquation: 3 H2O2 + 2 Cr(OH)SO4 + Base -> 2 CrO4(2-) (Carcinogenic Cr(VI)) + 4 H2O + SO4(2-)
matrix.description: Redox reactions between oxidizers (H2O2, HNO3) and strong reducers (NaBH4, sulfites) are explosive. In tanneries, accidental contact between strong oxidizers and Basic Chromium Sulfate oxidizes non-carcinogenic Cr(III) into highly toxic, carcinogenic, and mutagenic Hexavalent Chromium Cr(VI).
matrix.segregationAction: Strict physical segregation of chromium tanning salts and sulfide liquors from peroxide bleach and nitric acid.
matrix.emergencyPrecautions: Test wastewater immediately for Cr(VI) if cross-contamination is suspected. Add ferrous sulfate / sodium metabisulfite to reduce back to Cr(III).
matrix.authoritativeSource: NOAA CAMEO Chemicals / EU REACH Annex XVII Restriction on Cr(VI)

matrix.hazardTitle: Explosive Hydrogen (H2) Gas Release & Violent Thermal Eruption
matrix.description: Water-reactive substances (Sodium borohydride, hydrides, acyl halides) react with moisture or water, evolving large volumes of flammable Hydrogen (H2) or toxic gases with extreme heat that ignites the evolved gas.
matrix.segregationAction: Store in airtight, hermetically sealed metal drums under dry inert gas. Keep in elevated, moisture-free storage rooms above flood levels.
matrix.emergencyPrecautions: Class D dry powder fire extinguisher mandatory. NEVER use water, foam, or halogenated extinguishers.
matrix.authoritativeSource: NOAA CAMEO Chemicals / NFPA 400 Water-Reactive Materials

matrix.hazardTitle: Cytotoxic Environmental Contamination & Regulatory Sewer Violation
matrix.chemicalEquation: Cytotoxic API + Municipal Drain -> High Aquatic Genotoxicity (EPA Violation)
matrix.description: Aqueous dilution does NOT eliminate antineoplastic toxicity. Discharging cytotoxic drugs (Cisplatin, Methotrexate, Doxorubicin) into water/sewer violates Clean Water Act standards and damages sewage biomes.
matrix.segregationAction: MANDATORY: USP <800> compliance requires routing all antineoplastic solutions into rigid Yellow Cytotoxic Biohazard Buckets for high-temperature incineration at 1100°C. Never pour down sinks.
matrix.emergencyPrecautions: Cytotoxic spill kit with absorbent pads, neutralizer, and double biohazard disposal bags required.
matrix.authoritativeSource: USP <800> Hazardous Drugs / EPA RCRA Subpart P

matrix.hazardTitle: FATAL: Rapid Liberation of Hydrogen Cyanide (HCN) Gas
matrix.description: Acidification of cyanides immediately releases volatile, lethal Hydrogen Cyanide gas, which inhibits cellular cytochrome c oxidase and causes fatal hypoxia within minutes.
matrix.segregationAction: CRITICAL: Cyanide solutions must be maintained at pH > 11 at all times. Store in locked toxic poison cabinet. Segregate rigorously from all acids.
matrix.emergencyPrecautions: Administer Cyanokit (hydroxocobalamin) immediately upon exposure. Mandatory HCN air monitors.
matrix.authoritativeSource: NOAA CAMEO Chemicals / CDC NIOSH Emergency Response Card

matrix.chemicalEquation: Ethanol + Organic Solvent -> Stable Organic Solution (No Chemical Reaction)
matrix.description: Alcohols and non-halogenated organic solvents are mutually miscible and do not exhibit dangerous chemical reactivity, but share high vapor pressure and flammability.
matrix.segregationAction: Co-storage permitted in Non-Halogenated Organic Solvent carboy/drum. Must be grounded and bonded during transfer to eliminate static sparks.
matrix.emergencyPrecautions: Ensure grounding clamps are attached prior to pouring.

matrix.chemicalEquation: Water + Water-Miscible Solvents -> Stable Aqueous Blend
matrix.description: Water reduces flashpoint hazards of water-miscible solvents (Ethanol, Isopropanol) without dangerous reactivity.
matrix.segregationAction: Can be collected in solvent recovery drums if solvent concentration > 20%, or directed to biological pre-treatment if biodegradable.
matrix.authoritativeSource: NOAA CAMEO Chemicals / EPA Effluent Guidelines
